name: Burgio 2020
question: In men with overactive bladder symptoms, does combined behavioral training and tolterodine–tamsulosin reduce voiding frequency more than either treatment alone?

design.blinding: Participants and interventionists unblinded; outcome scoring blinded
design.population: Community-dwelling men aged at least 40 years with urgency and at least nine voids per 24 hours, recruited at three outpatient clinics.
design.description: Three-site, two-stage, three-arm randomized superiority trial
design.locator: PMC Methods, Design, Participants and Screening, Randomization; Figure 1

verdictNote: Combined treatment beat drugs alone, but not behavioral training alone, at six weeks.
takeaway: In men with overactive bladder symptoms, six weeks of behavioral training plus tolterodine–tamsulosin reduced daily voiding frequency more than tolterodine–tamsulosin alone, but not more than behavioral training alone; after all groups received combined therapy, 12-week differences were not significant.

reports.label: Initial and stepped-treatment report
reports.citation: Burgio KL, Kraus SR, Johnson TM 2nd, et al. "Effectiveness of Combined Behavioral and Drug Therapy for Overactive Bladder Symptoms in Men: A Randomized Clinical Trial." *JAMA Intern Med.* 2020;180(3):411-419. doi:10.1001/jamainternmed.2019.6398
reports.followUp: Six-week randomized comparison; 12-week assessment after both monotherapy groups stepped up to combination treatment

results.measure: Mean voids per 24 hours after six weeks; unadjusted mean difference, combined minus tolterodine–tamsulosin
results.note: Difference is subtraction of reported means; P is the prespecified comparison adjusted for baseline frequency and age. Primary two-sided threshold P < .025 after Bonferroni correction. Behavioral training versus drugs alone: P < .001.
results.locator: PMC Results, Stage 1; Table 2; Methods, Statistical Analyses

results.measure: Mean voids per 24 hours after six weeks; unadjusted mean difference, combined minus behavioral training
results.note: Difference is subtraction of reported means; P is the prespecified comparison adjusted for baseline frequency and age. Primary two-sided threshold P < .025.
results.locator: PMC Results, Stage 1; Table 2; Methods, Statistical Analyses

results.measure: Mean episodes per night after six weeks
results.note: P is the overall between-group test adjusted for baseline and age.

results.measure: Mean score after six weeks; lower is less bother
results.note: P is the overall between-group test adjusted for baseline and age.

results.measure: Mean voids per 24 hours at 12 weeks, after all arms received combination treatment
results.note: P is the overall between-group test adjusted for baseline and age.

harms.label: No adverse effects or none bothersome at six weeks
harms.note: Patient-rated adverse-effect bother; overall P < .001. Denominators are respondents to this item, not randomized arm sizes.

harms.label: Extremely bothersome adverse effects at six weeks
harms.note: Patient-rated adverse-effect bother; Table 3 reports percentages rounded to whole numbers.

delivery.label: Outcome assessment
delivery.value: Seven-day bladder diaries at baseline and after each six-week treatment stage.
delivery.locator: PMC Methods, Participants and Screening; Measurement

delivery.label: Behavioral treatment
delivery.value: Three clinic visits over six weeks; palpation-guided pelvic floor muscle training, urge suppression, delayed voiding, and daily diaries; home practice of 45 contractions daily in three sets of 15.
delivery.locator: PMC Methods, Interventions, Stage 1: Behavioral Therapy Alone

delivery.label: Drug regimen
delivery.value: Sustained-release tolterodine 4 mg daily plus tamsulosin 0.4 mg nightly; tolterodine could be reduced to 2 mg daily for tolerability.
delivery.locator: PMC Methods, Interventions, Stage 1: Drug Therapy Alone

delivery.label: Stage 1 completion
delivery.locator: PMC Results, Overview of Participant Flow; Figure 1
delivery.note: 183/204 completed treatment and the stage 1 assessment; 21 discontinued treatment.
